translations.literal: Tie Xuan was a man of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Xuan came from Deng.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，由國子生授禮科給事中，調都督府斷事。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu reign he entered service as a National University student, was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites section, and was transferred to be an adjudicator in the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu era he rose from the Imperial University to a supervising secretary in the Rites section, then was transferred to serve as an adjudicator in the Chief Military Commission.

translations.literal: Once he reported on a doubtful criminal case and at once made it clear.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he reviewed a doubtful criminal case and resolved it on the spot.

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was pleased and gave him the style name "Ding Shi" (Tripod Stone).
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor was delighted and bestowed on him the style Ding Shi, "Tripod Stone."

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign he became administration vice commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwen reign began he was appointed administration vice commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 李景隆之北伐也，鉉督餉無乏。

translations.literal: When Li Jinglong marched north, Xuan supervised supplies without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Jinglong's northern campaign, Xuan kept the supply lines running without fail.

sentences.zh: 景隆兵敗白溝河，單騎走德州，城戍皆望風潰。

translations.literal: Jinglong's army was defeated at the White Ditch River; he fled alone on horseback to Dezhou, and the garrisons in the city scattered at the sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinglong's army was routed at the White Ditch River, he fled alone on horseback to Dezhou, and every garrison in the city broke and fled at the first alarm.

sentences.zh: 鉉與參軍高巍感奮涕泣，自臨邑趨濟南，偕盛庸、宋參軍等誓以死守。

translations.literal: Xuan and staff officer Gao Wei were stirred and wept with tears; from Linyi they hurried to Jinan, and together with Sheng Yong, Staff Officer Song, and others swore to defend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and his staff officer Gao Wei, moved to tears, rushed from Linyi to Jinan and, with Sheng Yong, Staff Officer Song, and others, swore to hold the city to the last.

sentences.zh: 燕兵攻德州，景隆走依鉉。

translations.literal: The Yan army attacked Dezhou; Jinglong fled to rely on Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces attacked Dezhou, Jinglong fled to join Xuan.

sentences.zh: 德州陷，燕兵收其儲蓄百余萬，勢益張。

translations.literal: Dezhou fell; the Yan army seized more than a million in stored goods, and their momentum grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhou fell, and the Yan army seized stores worth more than a million taels, swelling their strength still further.

sentences.zh: 遂攻濟南，景隆復大敗，南奔。

translations.literal: They then attacked Jinan; Jinglong was again heavily defeated and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to Jinan; Jinglong suffered another crushing defeat and fled south.

translations.literal: Xuan and Yong and the others mounted the walls to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, Yong, and their comrades manned the walls to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 燕兵堤水灌城，築長圍，晝夜攻擊。

translations.literal: The Yan army dammed water to flood the city, built a long encirclement, and attacked day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan forces dammed the waters to flood Jinan, threw up a long siege line, and assaulted the walls without pause by day or night.

sentences.zh: 鉉以計焚其攻具，間出兵奮擊。

translations.literal: Xuan by stratagem burned their siege engines and from time to time sent troops out to strike fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan set fire to their siege engines by ruse and sent sorties to strike back whenever he could.

translations.literal: He also sent a thousand men out of the city to feign surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a thousand men outside the walls to pretend surrender.

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan was greatly pleased, and throughout the army all cheered.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan was overjoyed, and cheers rang through the camp.

sentences.zh: 鉉伏壯士城上，候王入，下鐵板擊之。

translations.literal: Xuan hid strong men on the wall, waiting for the prince to enter, then to drop an iron plate to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan posted braves atop the wall to wait until the prince entered the gate, then drop an iron portcullis upon him.

translations.literal: He set ambushes separately and cut the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He laid further ambushes and prepared to cut the bridge.

sentences.zh: 既而失約，王未入城板驟下。

translations.literal: Before long the plan missed its timing; the prince had not entered the city when the plate suddenly dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The timing slipped; before the prince had entered the gate the portcullis crashed down.

sentences.zh: 王驚走，伏發，橋倉卒不可斷，王鞭馬馳去。

translations.literal: The prince fled in alarm; the ambush was sprung, but the bridge could not be cut in haste; the prince whipped his horse and galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: The prince bolted in alarm as the ambush sprang, but the bridge could not be severed in time; he lashed his horse and raced away.

translations.literal: Furious, he attacked by every stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, he threw every means of assault against the city.

sentences.zh: 凡三閱月，卒固守不能下。

translations.literal: For three months in all, they held firm to the end and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: For three full months the defenders held fast, and the city could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 當是時，平安統兵二十萬，將復德州，以絕燕餉道。

translations.literal: At that time Ping An commanded two hundred thousand troops and was about to recover Dezhou, to cut off the Yan supply route.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Ping An was leading two hundred thousand men to retake Dezhou and sever the Yan supply line.

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan was afraid and lifted the siege to return north.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing this threat, the Prince of Yan raised the siege and marched back north.

sentences.zh: 燕王自起兵以來，攻真定二日不下，即舍去。

translations.literal: Since the Prince of Yan had raised his army, when he attacked Zhending for two days without taking it he at once abandoned it.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he took up arms, the Prince of Yan had never lingered: if a place such as Zhending held out for two days, he moved on.

sentences.zh: 獨以得濟南，斷南北道，即畫疆守，金陵不難圖。

translations.literal: He regarded gaining Jinan alone, cutting the north-south road, as drawing boundaries to hold; Jinling would not be hard to scheme for.
translations.idiomatic: He judged that holding Jinan and severing the north-south corridor would let him fix his frontier and make Jinling an easy prize.

sentences.zh: 故乘大破景隆之銳，盡力以攻，期於必拔，而竟為鉉等所挫。

translations.literal: Therefore, riding the sharp edge of his great defeat of Jinglong, he exerted all strength to attack, expecting certain capture, yet in the end was thwarted by Xuan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: So, while his victory over Jinglong was still fresh, he threw his full strength into the siege, determined to take the city at all costs—yet Xuan and his fellows turned him back.

sentences.zh: 帝聞大悅，遣官慰勞，賜金幣，封其三世。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was greatly pleased; he sent officials to console and reward, bestowed gold and silk, and enfeoffed three generations of his family.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed at the news, sent envoys with rewards, granted gold and silks, and ennobled three generations of Xuan's kin.

translations.literal: Xuan entered to give thanks and was granted a feast.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan came to court to give thanks and was feasted by the throne.

translations.literal: Whatever he proposed in memorials was all adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Every proposal he submitted was accepted.

translations.literal: He was promoted to administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: The court raised him to administration commissioner of Shandong.

translations.literal: Soon he advanced to minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 以盛庸代景隆為平燕將軍，命鉉參其軍務。

translations.literal: Sheng Yong replaced Jinglong as Pacification General against Yan; the emperor ordered Xuan to take part in his military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong replaced Jinglong as Pacification General against Yan, and Xuan was ordered to share command of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，庸大敗燕王於東昌，斬其大將張玉。

translations.literal: That winter Yong heavily defeated the Prince of Yan at Dongchang and beheaded his great general Zhang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Yong routed the Prince of Yan at Dongchang and killed his chief general Zhang Yu.

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan fled back to Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan fled back to Beiping.

sentences.zh: 自燕兵犯順，南北日尋幹戈，而王師克捷，未有如東昌者。

translations.literal: Since the Yan army had violated the throne, north and south daily sought battle, yet among imperial victories none matched Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: From the day the Yan forces rose in rebellion, the realm had seen fighting every day, yet no victory of the imperial army had equaled Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 自是燕兵南下由徐、沛，不敢復道山東。

translations.literal: From then on the Yan army marched south by Xu and Pei, and did not dare again to take the Shandong route.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Yan forces marched south through Xu and Pei and no longer dared to pass through Shandong.

sentences.zh: 比燕兵漸逼，帝命遼東總兵官楊文將所部十萬與鉉合，絕燕後。

translations.literal: As the Yan army gradually pressed close, the emperor ordered the Liaodong regional commander Yang Wen to lead his hundred thousand troops to join Xuan and cut off the Yan rear.
translations.idiomatic: As the Yan advance drew nearer, the emperor ordered the Liaodong regional commander Yang Wen to march his hundred thousand men to join Xuan and strike at the Yan rear.

sentences.zh: 文師至直沽，為燕將宋貴等所敗，無一至濟南者。

translations.literal: Wen's army reached Zhigu and was defeated by the Yan generals Song Gui and others; not one man reached Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's column reached Zhigu, where Yan generals such as Song Gui routed it; not a single soldier reached Jinan.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，燕軍南綴王師於小河，鉉與諸將時有斬獲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, fourth month, the Yan army delayed the imperial army at the Small River in the south; Xuan and the generals from time to time had beheadings and captures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year the Yan army pinned the imperial forces at the Small River; Xuan and his fellow commanders still won occasional kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 連戰至靈璧，平安等師潰被擒。

translations.literal: Fighting in succession reached Lingbi; Ping An and the others' armies collapsed and were captured.
translations.idiomatic: After successive battles the armies reached Lingbi, where Ping An's forces broke and he was taken prisoner.

translations.literal: Before long Yong also suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sheng Yong was defeated as well.

sentences.zh: 燕兵渡江，鉉屯淮上，兵亦潰。

translations.literal: The Yan army crossed the river; Xuan garrisoned on the Huai, and his troops also collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces crossed the Yangzi, Xuan held the Huai line, but his army broke and fled.

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan assumed the imperial throne and had him seized and brought before him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Yan took the throne, Xuan was captured and brought into his presence.

sentences.zh: 反背坐廷中嫚罵，令其一回顧，終不可，遂磔於市。

translations.literal: He sat in the hall with his back turned, reviling insolently; they ordered him to turn his head once, but he would not to the end, and he was dismembered in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in court with his back to the throne, hurling abuse; though ordered to look around once, he refused to the last, and was torn apart in the public square.

translations.literal: His age was thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-seven years old.

translations.literal: His son Fu'an was garrisoned at Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu'an was sent to garrison Hechi.

sentences.zh: 父仲名，年八十三，母薛，並安置海南。

translations.literal: His father Zhongming, age eighty-three, and his mother Xue were both resettled on Hainan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongming, aged eighty-three, and his mother Xue were both exiled to Hainan.

translations.literal: As for Staff Officer Song, his personal name is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The staff officer surnamed Song—his given name is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 燕兵攻濟南不克，舍之南去。

translations.literal: The Yan army attacked Jinan without taking it and abandoned it to march south.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces failed to take Jinan, they left it and marched south.

translations.literal: The staff officer urged Xuan to strike straight at Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: The staff officer urged Xuan to march directly on Beiping.

translations.literal: Xuan, because the troops were extremely exhausted, did not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan judged the troops too worn down and did not act on the plan.

translations.literal: Later his end is not known.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing further is known of his fate.

translations.literal: Bao Zhao was a man of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Zhao came from Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，由國子生授大理寺司務。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu reign, from a National University student he was appointed clerk of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu era he rose from the Imperial University to a clerkship in the Court of Judicial Review.

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to right vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of the reign he was made right vice minister of justice.

translations.literal: The next year he advanced to minister.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 耿介有峻節，布衣麻履，以清儉知名。

translations.literal: Upright and stern in integrity, he wore plain cloth and hemp sandals and was known for purity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Fiercely upright, he dressed in plain cloth and hemp sandals and was famed for austerity.

sentences.zh: 建文初，充北平采訪使，得燕不法狀，密以聞，請預為備。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign he served as investigation commissioner for Beiping, obtained evidence of Yan's unlawful acts, reported secretly, and asked to prepare defenses in advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwen reign began he was sent as investigation commissioner to Beiping, uncovered the prince's illegal acts, reported them in secret, and urged the court to prepare defenses.

sentences.zh: 燕兵起，設平燕布政司於真定，昭以尚書掌司事，與鐵鉉輩悉心經畫。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, a Pacification of Yan administration commission was set up at Zhending; Zhao as minister directed its affairs and with Tie Xuan and his fellows planned with full care.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan rebellion broke out, a Pacification of Yan administration commission was established at Zhending; Zhao, as minister, directed it and worked closely with Tie Xuan and others to organize the defense.

translations.literal: When Ping An's armies were defeated, he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: After Ping An's forces were routed, he was recalled to court.

translations.literal: When the Jinchuan Gate fell, he fled but was seized.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jinchuan Gate fell he fled, but was captured.

translations.literal: He would not submit and was dismembered to death.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to yield and was torn apart.

sentences.zh: 繼昭為刑部尚書者侯泰，字順懷，南和人。

translations.literal: He who succeeded Zhao as minister of justice was Hou Tai, styled Shunhuai, a man of Nanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tai, styled Shunhuai, of Nanhe, succeeded Zhao as minister of justice.

translations.literal: He began his career by recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through recommendation.

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign he served up to minister.
translations.idiomatic: By the opening of the Jianwen reign he had risen to minister.

sentences.zh: 燕王舉兵，力主抗禦之策。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan raised his army, he strongly advocated policies of resistance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan rebelled, he forcefully urged a policy of all-out resistance.

translations.literal: He once supervised supplies at Jining and Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He had supervised grain transport at Jining and Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 京師不守，行至高郵，被執下獄，與弟敬祖，子玘，俱被殺。

translations.literal: When the capital could not be held, traveling as far as Gaoyou he was seized and imprisoned; with his younger brother Jingzu and son Qi, all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he fled as far as Gaoyou, where he was seized and thrown into prison; he, his younger brother Jingzu, and his son Qi were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 陳性善，名復初，以字行，山陰人。

translations.literal: Chen Xingshan, personal name Fuchu, known by his style, was a man of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xingshan, whose personal name was Fuchu but who was known by his style, came from Shanyin.

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the thirtieth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the thirtieth year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 臚唱過御前，帝見其容止凝重，屬目久之，曰：「君子也。」

translations.literal: When the palace announcement passed before the throne, the emperor saw his bearing grave and composed, fixed his gaze on him for a long while, and said: "A gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: As his name was called before the throne, the emperor noted his grave and composed bearing, watched him at length, and said, "Here is a gentleman."

sentences.zh: 授行人司副，遷翰林檢討。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice commissioner in the Foreign Envoys Office and transferred to Hanlin reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice commissioner in the Foreign Envoys Office, then promoted to Hanlin reviser.

sentences.zh: 性善工書，嘗召入便殿，繙錄誠意伯劉基子璉所獻其父遺書。

translations.literal: Xingshan was skilled at calligraphy; once he was summoned to the private hall to transcribe the posthumous writings of Lord of Sincerity Liu Ji's father, presented by his son Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshan excelled at calligraphy; on one occasion he was summoned to the private hall to copy the posthumous writings of Liu Ji's father, which Liu Ji's son Lian had presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝威嚴，見者多惴恐，至惶汗，不成一字。

translations.literal: The emperor was august; many who saw him were fearful and alarmed, even to panicked sweat, and could not form a single character.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's presence was so imposing that most who faced him trembled with fear, sweating in panic until they could not form a single character.

sentences.zh: 性善舉動安祥，字畫端好。

translations.literal: Xingshan's movements were tranquil and his characters upright and fine.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshan remained calm in manner, and his brushwork was steady and elegant.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜酒饌，留竟日出。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed wine and food, and kept him until the day ended before he left.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, gave him wine and a meal, and kept him until nightfall.

sentences.zh: 惠帝在東宮，習知性善名。

translations.literal: When the Huandi was in the Eastern Palace, he had learned Xingshan's name.
translations.idiomatic: The future Huandi, while still crown prince, had already heard of Xingshan's reputation.

sentences.zh: 及即位，擢為禮部侍郎，薦起流人薛正言等數人。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Xingshan was raised to vice minister of rites and recommended restoring several exiles such as Xue Zhengyan.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession he made Xingshan vice minister of rites and, on his recommendation, restored several banished officials including Xue Zhengyan.

sentences.zh: 雲南布政使韓宜可隸謫籍，亦以性善言，起副都御史。

translations.literal: Han Yike, administration commissioner of Yunnan, was entered on the register of banishment; also on Xingshan's word he was raised to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yike, administration commissioner of Yunnan, had been struck from office and banished; at Xingshan's urging he too was restored as vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝退朝，獨留性善賜坐，問治天下要道，手書以進。

translations.literal: One day the emperor left court, kept Xingshan alone and granted him a seat, asked the essential way to govern the realm, and submitted a memorial in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: One day, after court had adjourned, the emperor kept Xingshan behind, seated him, asked the essentials of governing the realm, and had him write out his answer by hand.

translations.literal: Whatever Xingshan said in full, all was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted every point Xingshan made.

sentences.zh: 已，為有司所格，性善進曰：「陛下不以臣不肖，猥承顧問。

translations.literal: Later, when blocked by the responsible offices, Xingshan advanced and said: "Your Majesty, not deeming your servant unworthy, has condescended to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the responsible offices blocked his proposals, Xingshan came forward and said, "Your Majesty, though I am unworthy, has honored me with his counsel.

translations.literal: Having presumptuously soiled the sacred ear, you promised your servant they would certainly be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Having deigned to hear me, Your Majesty promised that my advice would be carried out.

translations.literal: Before long they were halted and changed; the affair was like reversing sweat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet before long the orders were revoked—no different from breaking a sworn word.

translations.literal: How can the realm be trusted?"
translations.idiomatic: How is the realm to trust Your Majesty thereafter?

translations.literal: The emperor was moved in expression.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was visibly moved.

sentences.zh: 燕師起，改副都御史，監諸軍。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, he was changed to vice censor-in-chief to supervise the armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces rebelled he was made vice censor-in-chief and placed over the armies.

sentences.zh: 靈璧戰敗，與大理丞彭與明、欽天監副劉伯完等皆被執。

translations.literal: Defeated at Lingbi, with Court of Judicial Review aide Peng Yuming, Vice Director of the Astronomy Bureau Liu Bowan, and others, all were seized.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Lingbi he was captured, along with Court of Judicial Review aide Peng Yuming, Vice Director of the Astronomy Bureau Liu Bowan, and others.

translations.literal: Before long all were released to return.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 性善曰：「辱命，罪也，奚以見吾君？」

translations.literal: Xingshan said: "To disgrace one's commission is a crime—how can one face our lord?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingshan said, "To fail one's charge is a disgrace—how can I face my sovereign?

translations.literal: In court dress he leaped on a horse and entered the river to die.
translations.idiomatic: Still in court dress, he spurred his horse into the river and drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 余姚黃墀、陳子方與性善友，亦同死。

translations.literal: Huang Chi of Yuyao and Chen Zifang, friends of Xingshan, also died together.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chi of Yuyao and Chen Zifang, his friends, died with him.

sentences.zh: 燕王入京師，詔追戮性善，徙其家於邊。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan entered the capital, an edict pursued posthumous punishment of Xingshan and moved his family to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Yan took the capital, an edict condemned Xingshan posthumously and exiled his family to the borderlands.

translations.literal: Yuming was a man of Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yuming came from Wan'an.

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial University as a tribute student and served through supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial University as a tribute student and rose to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 建文初，為大理右丞，廉勤敏達。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign he was right aide of the Court of Judicial Review, pure, diligent, and quick in understanding.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianwen reign he served as right aide of the Court of Judicial Review, known for integrity, diligence, and sharp judgment.

translations.literal: Because he supervised the army he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: He was captured while supervising the army.

translations.literal: Released to return, in shame and anger he tore cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: After he was released, shame and rage drove him to tear his cap and robes.

sentences.zh: 變姓名，與伯完俱亡去，不知所終。

translations.literal: He changed his name and fled together with Bowan; their end is not known.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his name and fled with Bowan; nothing more is known of either man.

sentences.zh: 時以侍郎監軍者，有廬江陳植。

translations.literal: At that time among those who as vice ministers supervised the army was Chen Zhi of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Among the vice ministers then supervising the armies was Chen Zhi of Lujiang.

translations.literal: Zhi, at the end of the Yuan, passed the provincial examination but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had passed the provincial examination at the end of the Yuan but declined office.

translations.literal: In the Hongwu period he was a director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu he served as a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 建文二年官兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwen he was made right vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwen he was appointed right vice minister of war.

translations.literal: When the Yan army reached the river, Zhi supervised the battle on the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces reached the Yangzi, Zhi directed the defense on the river.

translations.literal: He swore the army with generous spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the troops with an impassioned oath.

sentences.zh: 部將有議迎降者，植責以大義，甚厲。

translations.literal: Among the subordinate generals some discussed welcoming surrender; Zhi rebuked them with righteous principle, very sternly.
translations.idiomatic: When some subordinates talked of surrender, Zhi rebuked them sternly in the name of loyalty.

translations.literal: The subordinate generals killed him to surrender and moreover asked for reward.
translations.idiomatic: They killed him and opened the gates, then demanded a reward.

sentences.zh: 燕王怒，立誅部將，具棺殮葬植白石山上。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan was angry, at once executed the subordinate generals, and provided a coffin to bury Zhi on White Stone Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan was enraged, had the mutineers executed at once, and gave Zhi an honorable burial on White Stone Mountain.

sentences.zh: 燕師之至江北也，御史王彬巡按江淮。

translations.literal: When the Yan army reached the north of the river, censor Wang Bin toured and inspected the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces reached the north bank of the Yangzi, Censor Wang Bin was touring the Jiang-Huai circuit.

sentences.zh: 駐揚州，與鎮撫崇剛嬰城堅守。

translations.literal: Stationed at Yangzhou, with regional commander Chong Gang he encircled the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: He held Yangzhou and, with regional commander Chong Gang, mounted a stubborn defense of the walls.

sentences.zh: 時盛庸兵既敗，人無固誌。

translations.literal: At that time Sheng Yong's army had already been defeated, and men had no firm will.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong's army had already been routed, and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 守將王禮謀舉城降，彬執之及其黨，系獄。

translations.literal: The defending general Wang Li plotted to surrender the whole city; Bin seized him and his faction and imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander Wang Li plotted to surrender the city; Bin arrested him and his accomplices and threw them in prison.

sentences.zh: 剛出練兵，彬修守具，晝夜不懈。

translations.literal: Gang went out to drill troops; Bin repaired defensive equipment, day and night without slack.
translations.idiomatic: While Gang drilled the troops outside, Bin repaired the defenses and kept watch day and night.

sentences.zh: 有力士能舉千斤，彬嘗以自隨。

translations.literal: There was a strong man able to lift a thousand jin; Bin often had him follow him.
translations.idiomatic: A strongman who could lift a thousand jin often accompanied him as a bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 燕兵飛書城中：「縛王御史降者，官三品。」

translations.literal: The Yan army sent a message into the city by arrow: "Whoever binds Censor Wang and surrenders will receive a third-rank office."
translations.idiomatic: The Yan forces shot a message into the city: "Whoever binds Censor Wang and surrenders will be given a third-rank post.

translations.literal: Those around feared the strong man and none dared act.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants feared the strongman and dared not move against Bin.

sentences.zh: 禮弟崇賂力士母，誘其子出。

translations.literal: Li's younger brother Chong bribed the strong man's mother and lured his son out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Li's younger brother Chong bribed the strongman's mother and lured the son away.

translations.literal: Taking advantage of Bin removing his armor to bathe, they suddenly bound him.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Bin unarmed while he was bathing and bound him.

translations.literal: They released Li from prison, opened the gate, and admitted the Yan army.
translations.idiomatic: They freed Wang Li from prison, opened the gates, and admitted the Yan army.

translations.literal: Bin and Gang both would not submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: Bin and Gang both refused to yield and were put to death.

translations.literal: Bin, styled Wenzhi, was a man of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, styled Wenzhi, came from Dongping.

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the Hongwu reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination under Hongwu.

translations.literal: Gang's native district is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Gang's place of origin is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 又兵部主事樊士信，應城人。

translations.literal: Also Ministry of War director Fan Shixin, a man of Yingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Another was Fan Shixin, a director in the Ministry of War, from Yingcheng.

sentences.zh: 守淮，力拒燕兵，不勝，死之。

translations.literal: Defending the Huai, he strove to resist the Yan army, was not victorious, and died for it.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Huai line, fought the Yan forces to the last, and died when the defense failed.

sentences.zh: 燕將張玉、朱能等帥勇士攻九門，克其八，獨西直門不下。

translations.literal: Yan generals Zhang Yu, Zhu Neng, and others led brave warriors to attack the Nine Gates, took eight of them, and only Xizhi Gate would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Yan generals Zhang Yu and Zhu Neng led picked warriors against the Nine Gates, took eight, and only Xizhi Gate held out.

sentences.zh: 都指揮彭二躍馬呼市中曰：「燕王反，從我殺賊者賞！」

translations.literal: Regional commander Peng Er leaped on his horse and shouted in the market: "The Prince of Yan has rebelled—whoever follows me to kill the traitors will be rewarded!"
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Peng Er galloped through the streets crying, "The Prince of Yan has rebelled—follow me and slay the traitors, and you shall be rewarded!

translations.literal: He gathered more than a thousand troops and was about to attack the Yan residence.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand men rallied to him, and they prepared to storm the prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 會燕健士從府中出，格殺二，兵遂散，盡奪九門。

translations.literal: Just then Yan stalwarts came out from the residence, killed Er in combat, the troops then scattered, and they seized all the Nine Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Yan stalwarts burst from the residence, cut Peng Er down in the fight, and the crowd scattered; the rebels then held all Nine Gates.

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bing was killed, the funeral could be returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Bing was first killed, his body was recovered for burial.

sentences.zh: 「靖難」後，出昺屍焚之，家人及近戚皆死。

translations.literal: After the "Pacification of Difficulties," Bing's corpse was exhumed and burned; his family and close kin all died.
translations.idiomatic: After the Pacification campaign, his corpse was dug up and burned, and his family and close relatives were all put to death.

translations.literal: Ge Cheng—by what path he advanced is not known.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Cheng's path into office is not recorded.

translations.literal: At the end of Hongwu he was chief steward of the Yan residence.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Hongwu reign he served as chief steward of the Yan princely establishment.

translations.literal: Once he received the prince's order to report affairs in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he was sent to the capital on the prince's business.

sentences.zh: 帝召見，問府中事，誠具以實對。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him for audience, asked about affairs in the residence, and Cheng reported everything truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him and questioned him about the princely household; Cheng answered fully and truthfully.

translations.literal: He was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent back to Beiping.

sentences.zh: 王佯病，盛暑擁爐坐，呼寒甚。

translations.literal: The prince feigned illness; in the height of summer he sat hugging a brazier, crying that he was very cold.
translations.idiomatic: The prince pretended to be ill; in midsummer he sat huddled over a brazier, complaining bitterly of the cold.

translations.literal: Bing, Gui, and the others entered to inquire after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Bing, Xie Gui, and the others came in to inquire after his health.

translations.literal: Cheng said: "The prince is in fact not ill and is about to make a revolt."]
translations.idiomatic: Cheng warned them, "The prince is not ill at all—he is preparing a rebellion.

translations.literal: He also sent a confidential memorial to inform the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a secret report to the emperor about the plot.

sentences.zh: 及昺、貴將圖王，誠與護衛指揮盧振約為內應。

translations.literal: When Bing and Gui were about to plot against the prince, Cheng and bodyguard commander Lu Zhen agreed to serve as inner accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bing and Xie Gui were preparing to move against the prince, Ge Cheng and Lu Zhen, commander of the princely guard, arranged to act as inside collaborators.

sentences.zh: 事敗，誠、振俱被殺，夷其族。

translations.literal: The affair failed; Cheng and Zhen were both killed, and their clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered; Ge Cheng and Lu Zhen were both executed, and their entire families were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 又伴讀余逢辰，字彥章，宣城人。

translations.literal: There was also a study companion, Yu Fengchen, styled Yanzhang, a native of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Another was the tutor-companion Yu Fengchen, courtesy name Yanzhang, from Xuancheng.

translations.literal: He possessed learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 王信任之，以故得聞異謀，乘間力諫。

translations.literal: The prince trusted him; for this reason he could hear of the secret plot, and he seized opportunities to urge strongly in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The prince trusted him, so he learned of the conspiracy and repeatedly seized chances to remonstrate with all his force.

sentences.zh: 知變將作，貽書其子，誓必死。

translations.literal: Knowing a revolt was about to break out, he sent a letter to his son, vowing he would certainly die.
translations.idiomatic: Foreseeing the coming rebellion, he wrote to his son and swore he would not survive it.

sentences.zh: 兵起，復泣諫，言「君、父兩不可負」，死之。

translations.literal: When troops rose, he again remonstrated weeping, saying "Liege and father—neither may one fail," and died for it.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out, he wept as he remonstrated once more, declaring that one owed duty both to ruler and to father, and died for his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 北平人杜奇者，才雋士也。

translations.literal: There was a man of Beiping named Du Qi, a talented and sharp gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qi of Beiping was a gifted and forceful scholar.

sentences.zh: 燕王起兵，徵入府，奇因極諫「當守臣節」，王怒，立斬之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan raised troops, he was summoned into the residence, and Qi therefore remonstrated to the utmost that "one ought to keep a minister's integrity"; the prince was angry and immediately beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan took up arms, Du Qi was summoned to the princely residence and passionately urged him to uphold a loyal subject's duty; the prince flew into a rage and had him beheaded on the spot.

translations.literal: Song Zhong—what place he came from is not known.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhong's origins are unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，為錦衣衛指揮使。

translations.literal: At the end of Hongwu he was commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Hongwu reign he served as commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 有百戶以非罪論死，忠疏救。

translations.literal: There was a company commander sentenced to death for a non-crime, and Zhong memorialized to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: When a company officer was condemned to death on a false charge, Song Zhong submitted a memorial in his defense.

sentences.zh: 御史劾之，太祖曰：「忠率直無隱，為人請命，何罪？」

translations.literal: A censor impeached him, and the Founding Emperor said: "Zhong is straight and hides nothing; he pleaded for another man's life—what crime is that?"]
translations.idiomatic: A censor impeached him for it, but the Founding Emperor said, "Song Zhong speaks plainly and without concealment; he was begging mercy for another man—where is the offense in that?

translations.literal: Thereupon the company commander was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The company officer was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 尋為僉都御史劉觀所劾，調鳳陽中衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was impeached by Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan and was transferred to be commander of the Fengyang Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan impeached him, and he was reassigned as commander of the Fengyang Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 三十年，平羌將軍齊讓征西南夷無功，以忠為參將，從將軍楊文討之。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Pacification General Qi Rang's campaign against the southwestern tribes achieved nothing; Zhong was made deputy general and followed General Yang Wen to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of the reign, after Pacification General Qi Rang failed against the southwestern tribes, Song Zhong was appointed deputy commander and joined General Yang Wen's punitive campaign.

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was reinstated in the Embroidered Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the expedition returned, he was restored to his post in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 忠之守懷來也，都指揮余瑱、彭聚、孫泰與俱。

translations.literal: When Zhong defended Huailai, Brigade Commanders Yu Zhen, Peng Ju, and Sun Tai were with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Zhong held Huailai, Brigade Commanders Yu Zhen, Peng Ju, and Sun Tai served under him.

translations.literal: When battle came, Zhen was captured and, refusing submission, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting Yu Zhen was taken prisoner; he refused to yield and was killed.

sentences.zh: 泰中流矢，血被甲，裹創力鬥，與聚俱沒於陣。

translations.literal: Tai was struck by a flying arrow; blood covered his armor; he bound his wound and fought fiercely, and he and Ju both perished in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tai took an arrow in mid-fight; blood soaked his armor, yet he bandaged the wound and fought on until he and Peng Ju both fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 當是時，諸將校為燕所俘者百余人，皆不肯降，以死。

translations.literal: At that time, of the officers captured by Yan, more than a hundred all refused to surrender and died for it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time more than a hundred captured officers and commanders likewise refused to submit and died rather than yield.

translations.literal: It is a pity that most names were not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Regrettably, most of their names have not come down to us.

translations.literal: Ma Xuan—likewise, what place he came from is not known.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xuan's background is likewise unknown.

translations.literal: He held the office of brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 宋忠之趨居庸，宣亦自薊州帥師赴北平。

translations.literal: When Song Zhong hastened toward Juyong, Xuan also led troops from Jizhou toward Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Zhong marched on Juyong Pass, Ma Xuan too led an army from Jizhou toward Beiping.

translations.literal: Hearing of the rebellion, he fled back.
translations.idiomatic: On news of the uprising he turned back.

sentences.zh: 燕王既克懷來，旋師欲南下。

translations.literal: After the Prince of Yan had taken Huailai, he turned his army and wished to march south.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Prince of Yan had captured Huailai, he wheeled his army around and prepared to drive south.

sentences.zh: 張玉進曰：「薊州外接大寧，多騎士，不取恐為後患。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yu advanced and said: "Jizhou borders Daling; it has many horsemen; if we do not take it, I fear it will become a later trouble."]
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu urged him onward, saying, "Jizhou lies beside Daling and fields many cavalry; if we leave it untaken, it may plague us later.

sentences.zh: 會宣發兵將攻北平，與燕兵戰公樂驛，敗歸，與鎮撫曾濬城守。

translations.literal: It happened that Xuan had sent troops intending to attack Beiping; they fought Yan troops at Gongle Post, were defeated and returned, and together with garrison commander Zeng Jun he defended the city.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Ma Xuan had mobilized to strike Beiping; his force met the Yan army at Gongle Post, was beaten back, and he joined Garrison Commander Zeng Jun in holding the city.

sentences.zh: 玉等往攻之，宣出戰被擒，罵不絕口，與濬俱死。

translations.literal: Yu and the others went to attack them; Xuan went out to fight, was captured, cursed without cease, and died together with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu and his comrades besieged the city; Ma Xuan sallied forth, was taken, and cursed them without pause until he and Zeng Jun were both killed.

sentences.zh: 燕兵之襲大寧也，守將都指揮卜萬與都督劉真、陳亨帥兵扼松亭關。

translations.literal: When Yan troops raided Daling, defending commander Bu Wan and Commissioners Liu Zhen and Chen Heng led troops to block Songting Pass.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yan assault on Daling, garrison commander Bu Wan and commissioners Liu Zhen and Chen Heng held Songting Pass with their troops.

translations.literal: Heng wished to surrender to Yan but feared Wan and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Heng wanted to defect to the Prince of Yan but feared Bu Wan and held back.

sentences.zh: 燕行反間，貽萬書，盛稱萬；

translations.literal: Yan carried out a counter-intelligence plot, sending Wan a letter lavishly praising Wan;
translations.idiomatic: The Yan side ran a counter-intelligence scheme, sending Bu Wan a letter that lavishly praised him;

translations.literal: and bitterly slandering Heng.
translations.idiomatic: while viciously denouncing Chen Heng.

sentences.zh: 厚賞所獲大寧卒，緘書衣中，俾密與萬。

translations.literal: They richly rewarded captured Daling soldiers, sealed the letter in their clothing, and had them secretly give it to Wan.
translations.idiomatic: They richly rewarded captured soldiers from Daling, hid the letter in their clothes, and had them deliver it secretly to Bu Wan.

sentences.zh: 故使同獲卒見之，亦縱去而不與賞。

translations.literal: They deliberately let fellow-captured soldiers see this, and also released them without giving reward.
translations.idiomatic: They made sure other captives saw this favor, then released those men without paying them.

translations.literal: Those who received no reward exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The men who went unrewarded reported what had happened.

translations.literal: Zhen and Heng searched the soldiers' clothes and obtained the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen and Chen Heng searched the men's clothing and found the letter.

translations.literal: Thereupon they seized Wan, imprisoned him until he died, and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Wan was arrested, died in prison, and his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 萬忠勇而死於間，論者惜之。

translations.literal: Wan was loyal and brave yet died through intrigue; commentators regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Wan was loyal and courageous yet died by treachery; observers mourned the waste of it.

sentences.zh: 及大寧陷，指揮使朱鑒力戰，不屈死。

translations.literal: When Daling fell, Commander Zhu Jian fought fiercely, refused submission, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Daling fell, Commander Zhu Jian fought to the end and died rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 寧府左長史石撰者，平定人。

translations.literal: There was Left Chief Secretary Shi Zhuan of the Ning princely establishment, a native of Pingding.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhuan, left chief secretary of the Ning princely household, was a native of Pingding.

translations.literal: He was famed for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for scholarship and moral standing.

sentences.zh: 燕王舉兵，撰輒為守禦計，每以臣節諷寧王，王亦心敬之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan raised troops, Zhuan repeatedly devised plans for defense and every time used a minister's integrity to exhort the Prince of Ning; the prince also inwardly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan rebelled, Shi Zhuan constantly drafted defensive plans and urged the Prince of Ning to uphold a subject's loyalty, which the prince came to respect in his heart.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，憤詈不屈，支解死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he cursed in rage, refused submission, and was dismembered to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he raged and cursed, would not yield, and was torn limb from limb.

translations.literal: Qu Neng, a native of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Neng was from Hefei.

sentences.zh: 父通，洪武中，累官都督僉事。

translations.literal: His father Tong, during Hongwu, rose cumulatively to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qu Tong rose during the Hongwu era to vice commissioner of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 能嗣官，以四川都指揮使從藍玉出大渡河擊西番，有功。

translations.literal: Neng inherited the office; as Sichuan brigade commander he followed Lan Yu out the Great River to strike the western barbarians and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Neng inherited his father's post and, as brigade commander of Sichuan, joined Lan Yu's campaign beyond the Dadu River against the western tribes with distinction.

sentences.zh: 又以副總兵討建昌叛酋月魯帖木兒，破之雙狼寨。

translations.literal: He also served as deputy commander-in-chief to suppress the rebellious chieftain of Jianchang, Yuelu Timur, and defeated him at Twin Wolf Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: As deputy commander-in-chief he also crushed the Jianchang rebel chief Yuelu Timur at Twin Wolf Stockade.

translations.literal: When Yan forces rose, he followed Li Jinglong on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan rebelled, he joined Li Jinglong's northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 攻北平，與其子帥精騎千余攻彰義門，垂克。

translations.literal: Attacking Beiping, he and his son led more than a thousand elite horsemen to assault the Zhangyi Gate and were on the verge of taking it.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Beiping he and his son led over a thousand crack cavalry against the Zhangyi Gate and nearly broke through.

sentences.zh: 景隆忌之，令候大軍同進。

translations.literal: Jinglong envied him and ordered him to wait for the main army to advance together.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinglong, jealous of his success, ordered him to hold back until the main force could advance with him.

translations.literal: Thereupon the Yan men drew water by night and poured it over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: That night the defenders doused the walls with water.

sentences.zh: 方大寒，冰凝不可登，景隆卒致大敗。

translations.literal: It was just deep cold; ice froze and one could not climb; Jinglong ultimately brought on a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the bitter cold the water froze solid; the walls could not be scaled, and Li Jinglong's delay turned into catastrophic defeat.

sentences.zh: 已，又從景隆進駐白溝河，與燕師戰。

translations.literal: Later, he again followed Jinglong to advance and encamp at the White Ditch River, fighting Yan forces.
translations.idiomatic: Later he rejoined Li Jinglong at the White Ditch River and clashed with the Yan army.

translations.literal: Father and son Neng fought fiercely; wherever they turned, enemies were swept aside.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son fought with devastating force and swept all before them.

translations.literal: The sun set; each side withdrew its troops.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk both armies broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明日復戰，燕王幾為所及。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again; the Prince of Yan was nearly reached by them.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again the next day, and the Prince of Yan barely escaped their pursuit.

sentences.zh: 王急佯招後軍以疑之，得脫去。

translations.literal: The prince urgently feigned summoning the rear army to make them doubt, and so got away.
translations.idiomatic: Desperately he feigned a call to his rear guard, sowing doubt long enough to break free.

sentences.zh: 薄暮，能復引眾搏戰，大呼「滅燕」，斬馘數百。

translations.literal: Near dusk, Neng again led masses in fierce combat, shouting greatly "Destroy Yan," and beheaded several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Toward evening Qu Neng rallied his men again, roaring "Destroy Yan!" as they cut down hundreds of enemy.

sentences.zh: 諸將俞通淵、滕聚復帥眾來會。

translations.literal: Generals Yu Tongyuan and Teng Ju again led masses to come and join.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Yu Tongyuan and Teng Ju brought fresh forces to join him.

translations.literal: Just then a whirlwind arose; the prince burst in and charged in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Then a whirlwind struck; the prince drove straight into their ranks and charged.

translations.literal: Father and son Neng died in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Neng and his son fell on the field.

translations.literal: Tongyuan and Ju both died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tongyuan and Teng Ju were killed as well.

translations.literal: More than ten thousand crack troops were altogether lost.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand of the empire's finest troops perished in a single blow.

translations.literal: From this the southern army did not recover its vigor.
translations.idiomatic: The southern army never regained its momentum after that.

sentences.zh: 時與北兵戰死者，有都指揮莊得、楚智、皂旗張等。

translations.literal: At the time among those who died fighting northern troops were Brigade Commanders Zhuang De, Chu Zhi, Soap-banner Zhang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Among those killed fighting the northern armies at this time were Brigade Commanders Zhuang De and Chu Zhi, Soap-banner Zhang, and others.

translations.literal: De had formerly served under Song Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang De had once served under Song Zhong.

translations.literal: In the defeat at Huailai, one army alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: After the disaster at Huailai, his was the only unit to come through intact.

sentences.zh: 後從盛庸戰夾河，斬燕將譚淵。

translations.literal: Later he followed Sheng Yong to fight at Jiahe and beheaded Yan general Tan Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He later fought under Sheng Yong at Jiahe and killed the Yan general Tan Yuan.

sentences.zh: 已而燕王以驍騎乘暮掩擊，得力戰，死。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Yan, with fierce cavalry, used dusk to launch a surprise attack; De fought hard and died.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Prince of Yan struck at dusk with his elite cavalry; Zhuang De fought to the end and was killed.

sentences.zh: 智，嘗從馮勝、藍玉出塞有功。

translations.literal: Zhi had once followed Feng Sheng and Lan Yu beyond the frontier with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Zhi had campaigned beyond the frontier under Feng Sheng and Lan Yu with distinction.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he defended Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianwen reign he garrisoned Beiping.

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to court.

translations.literal: When they campaigned against Yan, he led troops following Jinglong.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against the Prince of Yan began, he took the field under Li Jinglong.

sentences.zh: 戰輒奮勇，北人望旗幟股栗。

translations.literal: In battle he always fought fiercely; northerners seeing his banners trembled in the thighs.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with savage courage in every engagement, and northerners shook at the sight of his banners.

translations.literal: At this time his horse foundered, he was captured, and died.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion his horse went down; he was taken and killed.

translations.literal: Soap-banner Zhang—his given name is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Soap-banner Zhang's personal name has not survived.

sentences.zh: 或曰張能力挽千斤，每戰輒麾皂旗先驅，軍中呼「皂旗張」。

translations.literal: Some say Zhang was able to draw a thousand jin; in every battle he always waved a black banner as vanguard, and in the army they called him "Soap-banner Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: Some say he could draw a bow of a thousand jin; in every battle he led the charge under a black banner, and the army knew him only as Soap-banner Zhang.

translations.literal: At death he still grasped the banner and did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was still gripping his banner, upright to the last.

translations.literal: There was also a Commander Wang, a native of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Commander Wang from Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 常騎小馬，軍中呼「小馬王」。

translations.literal: He usually rode a small horse; in the army they called him "Little-horse Wang."
translations.idiomatic: He habitually rode a small pony, and his men called him Little Horse Wang.

sentences.zh: 戰白溝河被重創，脫胄付其仆曰：「吾為國捐軀，以此報家人。」

translations.literal: Fighting at the White Ditch River he received grave wounds; he removed his helmet and gave it to his servant, saying: "I am giving my body for the state; with this I repay my household."
translations.idiomatic: Badly wounded at the White Ditch River, he took off his helmet and handed it to his attendant, saying, "I die for the realm; take this home to my family.

translations.literal: He stood by his horse, planted his halberd, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He sat his horse upright, planted his halberd, and died on the spot.

translations.literal: The deaths of the two men were especially unusual, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The manner of those two men's deaths was especially remarkable.

sentences.zh: 又中牟楊本，初為太學生，通禽遁術，應募授錦衣鎮撫。

translations.literal: There was also Yang Ben of Zhongmu; at first he was an imperial academy student, mastered techniques of birds and concealment, responded to recruitment and was appointed garrison commander of the Embroidered Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ben of Zhongmu had been an imperial academy student and versed himself in arcane military arts; he enlisted and was made a garrison commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 從景隆討燕有功，景隆忌之，不以聞。

translations.literal: Following Jinglong to suppress Yan he had merit; Jinglong envied him and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself under Li Jinglong against the Prince of Yan, but Jinglong envied him and never reported his achievements.

sentences.zh: 尋劾景隆喪師辱國，遂以孤軍獨出，被擒，系北平獄，後被殺。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached Jinglong for losing the army and shaming the state; thereupon with a lone army he went out alone, was captured, was held in Beiping prison, and later was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized against Li Jinglong for losing the army and disgracing the realm, then marched out alone with a solitary force, was captured, imprisoned at Beiping, and later executed.

translations.literal: Zhang Lun—what place he came from is not known.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lun's origins are unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 河北諸衛指揮使也，勇悍負氣，喜觀古忠義事。

translations.literal: He was a commander of guards in Hebei; brave and fierce, proud in spirit, he loved reading ancient tales of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was a guard commander in Hebei, bold and proud, with a passion for tales of ancient loyalty and sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 馬宣自薊州起兵攻北平，不克，死。

translations.literal: Ma Xuan, from Jizhou, raised troops to attack Beiping, did not take it, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Xuan marched from Jizhou to attack Beiping, failed, and died.

sentences.zh: 倫發憤，合兩衛官帥所部南奔，結盟報國。

translations.literal: Lun burned with resentment; he joined two guard officers and led their units south in flight, swearing an oath to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged by Ma Xuan's fate, Zhang Lun rallied two guard officers, led their men south in flight, and bound themselves in an oath to serve the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 從李景隆、盛庸戰，皆有功。

translations.literal: Following Li Jinglong and Sheng Yong in battle, he had merit in each.
translations.idiomatic: He fought under Li Jinglong and Sheng Yong and earned credit in every engagement.

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan assumed the imperial throne, he summoned Lun to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Yan took the throne, he offered Zhang Lun terms of surrender.

sentences.zh: 倫笑曰：「張倫將自賣為丁公乎！」

translations.literal: Lun laughed and said: "Is Zhang Lun about to sell himself to become a Duke Ding!"]
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lun laughed and said, "Am I, Zhang Lun, to sell myself out like Ding Gong?

translations.literal: He died for it.
translations.idiomatic: He chose death instead.

translations.literal: When the capital fell, military officials all surrendered and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, the military officials one after another submitted.

sentences.zh: 從容就義者，倫一人而已。

translations.literal: He who calmly accepted righteousness and died—Lun alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lun alone met his end with calm resolve.

sentences.zh: 主簿唐子清、典史黃謙俱被執。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Tang Ziqing and magistrate's clerk Huang Qian were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Tang Ziqing and Magistrate's Clerk Huang Qian were both taken prisoner.

translations.literal: The Yan general wished to release Ziqing.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan commander meant to set Tang Ziqing free.

translations.literal: Ziqing said: "I wish to follow Lord Yan to the underworld."
translations.idiomatic: Tang Ziqing replied, "I would rather join Lord Yan in the grave below.

translations.literal: Thereupon he died for it.
translations.idiomatic: With that he chose death.

translations.literal: They sent Qian to Xuzhou to summon surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They dispatched Huang Qian to Xuzhou to offer terms of surrender.

translations.literal: Qian did not comply, and likewise died.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qian refused, and died as well.

translations.literal: There was also Xiang Pu, a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Xiang Pu, from Cixi.

translations.literal: He applied himself to learning and supported his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He studied hard while caring for his parents.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，以人才召見，知獻縣。

translations.literal: At the end of Hongwu, he was summoned as a man of talent and appointed magistrate of Xian County.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years of the Hongwu reign he was summoned for his ability and made magistrate of Xian County.

sentences.zh: 縣無城郭，燕將譚淵至，樸集民兵與戰，被執，懷印死。

translations.literal: The county had no walls; when Yan general Tan Yuan arrived, Pu gathered militia to fight, was captured, and clutching the seal died.
translations.idiomatic: The county had no fortifications. When the Yan commander Tan Yuan arrived, Xiang Pu rallied the militia to resist; taken prisoner, he died clutching the official seal.

translations.literal: Zheng Shu, a native of Xianju.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shu was a native of Xianju.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Xiao County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Xiao County.

translations.literal: Yan general Wang Cong took Xiao; Shu would not submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan commander Wang Cong stormed Xiao, Zheng Shu refused to yield and was killed.

translations.literal: His two daughters were about to be distributed as spoils; they likewise died for it.
translations.idiomatic: When his two daughters were marked out for distribution as war spoils, they too chose death.

translations.literal: Zheng Hua, a native of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hua was from Linhai.

translations.literal: From Messenger he was demoted to clerk of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Having served as a Messenger, he was demoted to a minor clerk in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 燕兵至，州長貳盡棄城走。

translations.literal: When Yan troops arrived, the prefect and his deputies all abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army arrived, the prefect and his deputies abandoned the city and fled.

translations.literal: Hua said to his wife Xiao: "By my sense of duty, I must die.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hua told his wife Xiao, "My duty leaves me no choice but to die.

translations.literal: But you are still young—what of that?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are still so young—what will become of you?

sentences.zh: 蕭泣曰：「君不負國，妾敢負君？」

translations.literal: Xiao wept and said: "You refuse to betray the state—how could I dare betray you?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao wept and said, "You will not betray your country—how could I betray you?

translations.literal: Hua said: "That is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hua said, "That is enough.

sentences.zh: 帥吏民憑城固守，城破，力戰，不屈死。

translations.literal: He led officials and people to hold the walls; when the city fell he fought fiercely and died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied officials and townspeople to hold the walls; when the city fell he fought to the last and died without submitting.

translations.literal: Wang Sheng, style Zizhi, a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sheng, styled Zizhi, was a native of Jishui.

translations.literal: In Hongwu year five he took the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongwu he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 至京，詔免會試，命吏部授官。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital, an edict exempted him from the metropolitan exam and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to appoint him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital, an edict exempted him from the palace examination and the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to assign him a post.

translations.literal: Sheng said his parents were elderly and asked to return home to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sheng said his parents were old and asked to go home to care for them.

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned again for his literary attainments.

translations.literal: The founding emperor tested him personally; he pleased the throne and was to receive exceptional promotion.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor examined him in person; he pleased the throne and was marked for exceptional promotion.

translations.literal: He declared himself "talent thin, parents elderly" and asked for a convenient post near home.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded that his "talents were slight and his parents aged," and asked for a post convenient for supporting them.

translations.literal: He was appointed instructor at Fuliang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made instructor at Fuliang.

sentences.zh: 凡三為教官，最後得濟陽。

translations.literal: Three times he served as instructor; at last he was assigned to Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served three times as a school instructor and at last was posted to Jiyang.

translations.literal: When Yan troops arrived, he was seized by a roving patrol.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army arrived, he was captured by a roving detachment.

translations.literal: Calmly he drew parallels; his words were generous and resolute in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke calmly and by apt analogy, his words ringing with generous resolve.

translations.literal: The crowd let him go.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers released him.

sentences.zh: 歸坐明倫堂，伐鼓聚諸生，謂曰：「若等知此堂何名，今日君臣之義何如？」

translations.literal: Returning he sat in the Hall of Bright Virtue, beat the drum to gather students, and said: "Do you know what this hall is called, and what the lord-and-subject obligation is today?"
translations.idiomatic: Back at the Hall of Bright Virtue he beat the drum to assemble his students and asked, "Do you know why this hall bears its name, and what the bond between ruler and subject demands today?

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept greatly, and the students wept too.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into loud weeping, and his students wept with him.

translations.literal: Sheng dashed his head against a pillar and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sheng dashed his head against a pillar and died.

sentences.zh: 女靜，適即墨主簿周岐鳳。

translations.literal: His daughter Jing was married to Zhou Qifeng, registrar of Jimo.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter Jing had married Zhou Qifeng, registrar of Jimo.

sentences.zh: 聞燕兵至濟陽，知父必死，三遣人往訪，得遺骸歸葬。

translations.literal: Hearing Yan troops had reached Jiyang, she knew her father must die; three times she sent men to inquire, recovered his remains, and returned to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: When she heard the Yan army had reached Jiyang she knew her father would not survive; three times she sent men to search for him, recovered his body, and brought it home for burial.

translations.literal: Yao Shan, style Keyi, a native of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shan, styled Keyi, was a native of Anlu.

translations.literal: At first his surname was Li.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally borne the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 洪武中由鄉舉歷祁門縣丞，同知廬州、重慶二府。

translations.literal: During Hongwu, via provincial examination he served as assistant magistrate of Qimen, then vice-prefect of Luzhou and Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign he entered service through the provincial examination, serving as assistant magistrate of Qimen and then as vice-prefect of Luzhou and Chongqing.

translations.literal: In year thirty he was transferred to Suzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was transferred to prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖以吳俗奢僭，欲重繩以法，黠者更持短長相攻訐。

translations.literal: Initially the founding emperor, seeing Wu customs extravagant and presumptuous, wished to bind them strictly by law; the cunning then seized one another's faults to attack and denounce.
translations.idiomatic: At first the founding emperor, finding Wu customs extravagant and overreaching, meant to restrain them with stern law; the shrewd then seized on one another's faults to denounce and attack.

sentences.zh: 善為政持大體，不為苛細，訟遂衰息，吳中大治。

translations.literal: Shan governed grasping the larger principles, not pursuing petty minutiae; lawsuits then declined and quieted, and Wu was greatly well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shan governed by the broad principles of statecraft, not by petty exactitude; lawsuits dwindled and Suzhou was brought to good order.

sentences.zh: 好折節下士，敬禮隱士王賓、韓奕、俞貞木、錢芹輩。

translations.literal: He loved to lower himself before scholars and respectfully honored recluses Wang Bin, Han Yi, Yu Zhenmu, Qian Qin, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He humbled himself before men of learning and treated the recluses Wang Bin, Han Yi, Yu Zhenmu, Qian Qin, and others with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 以月朔會學宮，迎芹上座，請質經義。

translations.literal: On the first of each month he met at the academy, seated Qin in the place of honor, and asked him to expound the classics.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of each month he gathered at the academy, seated Qian Qin in the place of honor, and invited him to examine the meaning of the classics.

translations.literal: Qin said: "This is not what is urgent now."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Qin said, "That is not what matters most now.

translations.literal: Shan started up in alarm and asked.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shan started up in alarm and pressed him to explain.

translations.literal: Qin then handed him a booklet.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Qin then handed him a booklet.

translations.literal: Looking at it, it was all strategies for defense.
translations.idiomatic: When he opened it, he found it filled with plans for defense and garrison.

sentences.zh: 時燕兵已南下，密結鎮、常、嘉、松四郡守，練民兵為備。

translations.literal: At the time Yan troops had already marched south; he secretly joined with the prefects of Zhen, Chang, Jia, and Song prefectures, drilling militia to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Yan army was marching south; he secretly coordinated with the prefects of Zhenjiang, Changzhou, Jiaxing, and Songjiang, drilling militia in readiness.

translations.literal: He recommended Qin at court and had him appointed provisional judge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Qian Qin to the court and had him appointed provisional judge of military affairs.

translations.literal: Shan soon went to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shan soon went to the capital himself.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷以燕王上書貶齊泰、黃子澄於外，善言不當貶，遂復召二人。

translations.literal: It happened the court, in response to the Prince of Yan's memorial, demoted Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng to outside posts; Shan said they ought not be demoted, and the two were then recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When the court, responding to the Prince of Yan's memorial, demoted Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng to distant posts, Yao Shan argued they should not be removed and both men were recalled.

sentences.zh: 建文四年詔兼督蘇、松、常、鎮、嘉興五府兵勤王。

translations.literal: In Jianwen year four an edict made him concurrently supervise the five prefectures Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, and Jiaxing in raising troops to aid the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianwen an edict put him in charge of raising troops from Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, and Jiaxing to rescue the throne.

translations.literal: Before the troops were assembled, the Prince of Yan had already entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before the armies could gather, the Prince of Yan had already entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 時子澄匿善所，約共航海起兵。

translations.literal: At the time Zicheng was hidden at Shan's residence, and they agreed to put to sea together and raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zicheng was then in hiding at Yao Shan's house, and they agreed to put to sea together and raise a force.

sentences.zh: 善謝曰：「公，朝臣，當行收兵圖興復。

translations.literal: Shan declined, saying: "Sir, you are a court minister; you should go gather troops and plot restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shan declined, saying, "You are a minister of the court; you should go gather troops and plan restoration.

translations.literal: I guard the soil—it is enough to live or die with the city."
translations.idiomatic: I am bound to the land I govern; it is enough that I live or die with this city.

sentences.zh: 子澄去，善為麾下許千戶者縛以獻，不屈，死。

translations.literal: Zicheng left; Shan was bound by a centurion named Xu under his command and presented as captive; he would not submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zicheng departed; a centurion named Xu under Yao Shan's command bound him and handed him over. He refused to submit and was put to death.

translations.literal: Age forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-three years old.

translations.literal: His sons Jie and three others were all sent to frontier service as convicts.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jie and three others were all sent into frontier exile as convicts.

translations.literal: Qin, style Jizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Qin, styled Jizhong.

translations.literal: In youth he loved unusual integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was drawn to uncommon acts of integrity.

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan he approached various generals but found no recognition.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he sought out one general after another but won no appointment.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，辟大都督府掾，從中山王出北平至大漠。

translations.literal: At the start of Hongwu he was recruited as clerk to the Chief Military Commission, followed the Prince of Zhongshan north from Beiping to the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Hongwu he was recruited as a clerk in the Chief Military Commission and followed the Prince of Zhongshan from Beiping into the northern desert.

translations.literal: On return he resigned his office.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he resigned his post.

translations.literal: At home twenty years, content in poverty, delighting in the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for twenty years, content in poverty and devoted to the Way.

translations.literal: Through Shan's recommendation he was raised up.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shan's recommendation brought him back into service.

sentences.zh: 從李景隆北行，遣入奏事。

translations.literal: Following Li Jinglong north, he was sent to memorialize at court.
translations.idiomatic: He marched north with Li Jinglong and was dispatched to the capital to report on affairs.

translations.literal: Stricken on the road and near death, he still itemized and submitted military matters.
translations.idiomatic: Stricken on the road and near death, he still set down his views on military affairs in a memorial.

translations.literal: Age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-three years old.

translations.literal: Chen Yanhui, style Shiyuan, a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yanhui, styled Shiyuan, was a native of Putian.

sentences.zh: 父立誠，為歸安縣丞，被誣論死。

translations.literal: His father Licheng served as assistant magistrate of Guian and, falsely accused, was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: His father Licheng had been assistant magistrate of Guian; falsely accused, he was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 彥回謫戍雲南，家人從者多道死。

translations.literal: Yanhui was banished to serve garrison duty in Yunnan; of the family who followed, many died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yanhui was banished to garrison duty in Yunnan; of the family members who followed him, many died on the road.

sentences.zh: 比至蜀，唯彥回與祖母郭在。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Shu, only Yanhui and his grandmother Guo remained.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Shu, only Chen Yanhui and his grandmother Guo were left alive.

sentences.zh: 會赦，又弗原，監送者憐而縱之。

translations.literal: An amnesty came, yet he was not pardoned; the escort took pity and released him.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was proclaimed, but he was not included; the escort took pity on him and set him free.

sentences.zh: 貧不能歸，依鄉人知縣黃積良，冒黃姓。

translations.literal: Too poor to return home, he relied on fellow townsman Magistrate Huang Jiliang and took the Huang surname.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to go home, he stayed with a fellow townsman, Magistrate Huang Jiliang, and took the Huang surname.

sentences.zh: 久之，以閬中教諭嚴德政薦，授保寧訓導。

translations.literal: After a long while, through the recommendation of Yan Dezheng, instructor of Langzhong, he was appointed assistant instructor at Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: In time, on the recommendation of Yan Dezheng, instructor at Langzhong, he was appointed assistant instructor at Baoning.

sentences.zh: 考滿至京，召見以為平江知縣。

translations.literal: When his term review ended he went to the capital, was summoned and appointed magistrate of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he went to the capital, was received in audience, and was made magistrate of Pingjiang.

translations.literal: The next year the founding emperor died; Yanhui went to attend the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the founding emperor died, and Chen Yanhui went to the capital to mourn.

sentences.zh: 又以給事中楊維康薦，擢徵州知府。

translations.literal: Again through Supervising Secretary Yang Weikang's recommendation he was promoted to Huizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Supervising Secretary Yang Weikang he was promoted to prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 建文元年，以循良受上賞。

translations.literal: In Jianwen year one he received high reward as a model official.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwen he received high honors as a model official.

sentences.zh: 祖母郭卒，當去，百姓走京師乞留。

translations.literal: Grandmother Guo died; he was due to leave; the people ran to the capital to beg he remain.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandmother Guo died he was obliged to leave office, but the people rushed to the capital to beg that he be kept on.

sentences.zh: 彥回衰糸至赴闕自陳，乞復姓。

translations.literal: Yanhui came to court in mourning garb to report himself and beg restoration of his surname.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yanhui came to court in mourning garb to confess his case and beg to resume his own surname.

sentences.zh: 當彥回之戍雲南也，其弟彥亦戍遼東。

translations.literal: When Yanhui was garrisoned in Yunnan, his younger brother Yan was also garrisoned in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yanhui had been sent to garrison Yunnan, his younger brother Yan had also been sent to garrison Liaodong.

translations.literal: Now an edict cleared Yan from the register.
translations.idiomatic: At this point an edict removed Yan from the convict register.

translations.literal: Repeatedly he begged to complete mourning; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to complete the full mourning period, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 葬郭徽城北十里北山之陽。

translations.literal: He buried Guo on the sunny south slope of North Mountain, ten li north of Huizhou city.
translations.idiomatic: He buried her on the sunny southern slope of North Mountain, ten li north of Huizhou city.

translations.literal: Often he ran to the grave and wept with deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: He often ran to the grave and wept with piercing grief.

translations.literal: People pointed to it and called it "Prefect's Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: People came to call the place Prefect's Mountain.

sentences.zh: 嘗對百姓泣曰：「吾罪人也，向亡命冒他姓。
