translations.literal: Once facing the people he wept and said: "I am a guilty man; once a fugitive I took another surname.
translations.idiomatic: Once, facing the people, he wept and said, "I am a guilty man; once a fugitive I took another man's surname.

sentences.zh: 以祖母存，恐陳首獲罪，隱忍二十年。

translations.literal: Because grandmother lived, fearing confession would bring punishment, I endured in silence twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: While my grandmother lived I feared that if I came forward I would be punished, and so I bore it in silence for twenty years.

translations.literal: Now grandmother is gone; I ought to ask for death myself.
translations.idiomatic: Now that my grandmother is gone, I ought to ask for death myself.

sentences.zh: 上特宥我，終當死報國耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor specially pardoned me; in the end I must die repaying the state."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has specially spared me; in the end I can repay the realm only with my death.

sentences.zh: 燕兵逼京師，彥回糾義勇赴援。

translations.literal: When Yan troops pressed the capital, Yanhui rallied volunteers and rushed to aid.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army closed on the capital, Chen Yanhui gathered volunteers and marched to the rescue.

translations.literal: Soon after he was captured, shackled to the capital, and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was captured, bound in fetters, and taken to the capital, where he was executed.

translations.literal: Zhang Yanfang, a native of Longquan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanfang was a native of Longquan.

sentences.zh: 初為給事中，以便養乞改樂平知縣。

translations.literal: At first a supervising secretary; he asked to transfer to magistrate of Leping to be near his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served as a supervising secretary, then asked to be transferred to magistrate of Leping so he could care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 應詔勤王，帥所部抵湖口。

translations.literal: Answering the edict to aid the throne, he led his force to Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: Answering the call to rescue the throne, he led his command to Hukou.

translations.literal: He was captured, shackled, brought to Leping, and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He was taken prisoner, bound in fetters, brought to Leping, and executed.

translations.literal: His head was displayed on the drum tower.
translations.idiomatic: His head was put on display atop the watchtower.

sentences.zh: 當署月，一蠅不集，經旬面如生。

translations.literal: For a full month it hung there; not one fly gathered on it, and for ten days his face looked as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: For a month not a single fly settled on it; for ten days his face still looked as though he lived.

translations.literal: The people of the district secretly interred him behind the Hall of Pure White.
translations.idiomatic: Local people stole his body away and buried it behind the Hall of Pure White.

sentences.zh: 同時以勤王死者，有松江同知，死尤烈雲。

translations.literal: Among those who died at the same time answering the call to aid the throne was a vice-prefect of Songjiang; his death was especially fierce, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time a Songjiang vice-prefect died rallying to the throne; the manner of his death was said to have been especially heroic.

sentences.zh: 同知姓名不可考，或曰周繼瑜也。

translations.literal: The vice-prefect's name cannot be verified; some say it was Zhou Jiyu.
translations.idiomatic: His name is unrecorded; some identify him as Zhou Jiyu.

sentences.zh: 勤王詔下，榜募義勇入援。

translations.literal: When the edict to aid the throne was issued, he posted notices recruiting volunteers to enter as relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the call to rescue the throne went out, he posted notices to recruit volunteers for the march to the capital.

translations.literal: He spoke at length of great righteousness and moved men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with force on behalf of the dynasty and stirred the hearts of the people.

translations.literal: He also denounced the "Pacification of Difficulties" army for turning against grace and violating the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He also denounced the Prince of Yan's "Pacification of Difficulties" forces for betraying imperial favor and violating moral duty.

translations.literal: Bound in fetters he was taken to the capital and dismembered in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Shackled and brought to the capital, he was torn apart in the public square.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：燕師之南向也，連敗二大將，其鋒蓋不可當。

translations.literal: The annalist says: When the Yan army marched south, having defeated two great generals in succession, its momentum could not be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: The annalist writes: When the Yan army turned south, having routed two great commanders in succession, its momentum seemed irresistible.

sentences.zh: 鐵鉉以書生竭力抗禦於齊、魯之間，屢挫燕眾。

translations.literal: Tie Xuan, a literatus, exerted himself to resist between Qi and Lu and repeatedly checked the Yan forces.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Xuan, a scholar-official, threw himself into the defense between Qi and Lu and repeatedly turned back the Yan armies.

sentences.zh: 設與耿、李易地而處，天下事固未可知矣。

translations.literal: If he had exchanged places with Geng and Li, the affairs of the realm would indeed have remained uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: Had Geng Bingxin and Li Jinglong been placed in his position instead, the fate of the realm might well have remained in doubt.

sentences.zh: 張昺、謝貴、葛誠圖燕於肘腋，而事不就。

translations.literal: Zhang Bing, Xie Gui, and Ge Cheng plotted against Yan at close quarters, yet the affair did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bing, Xie Gui, and Ge Cheng plotted against the Prince of Yan from within his own household, yet their plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 宋忠、馬宣東西繼敗，瞿能諸將垂勝戰亡，燕兵卒得長驅南下。

translations.literal: Song Zhong and Ma Xuan were defeated in turn east and west; Qu Neng and other generals died in battle on the verge of victory, and the Yan army at last swept south unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhong and Ma Xuan fell in defeat one after another east and west; Qu Neng and other commanders died in battle on the brink of victory, and the Yan forces at last drove south without hindrance.

sentences.zh: 而姚善、陳彥回之屬，欲以郡邑之甲奮拒於大勢已去之後，此黃鉞所謂「兵至江南，禦之無及」者也。

translations.literal: Yet Yao Shan, Chen Yanhui, and men of their kind sought with the armor of counties and prefectures to resist fiercely after the great tide had already turned—this is what Huang Quan meant by "When the army reaches Jiangnan, there will be no time left to defend."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yao Shan, Chen Yanhui, and men like them tried to rally the arms of county and prefecture to resist after the tide had already turned—precisely the situation Huang Quan had in mind when he wrote, "When the army reaches Jiangnan, it will be too late to defend."
